drivingQuestion: From where is it derived that months are not counted to the Temple treasury's disadvantage?
outcomeNote: The mishna's rule is grounded in the phrase according to the years that remain.

segments.he: אֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין חֳדָשִׁים וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין חֳדָשִׁים עִם הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְחִשַּׁב לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַכֶּסֶף עַל פִּי הַשָּׁנִים הַנּוֹתָרוֹת״ — שָׁנִים אַתָּה מְחַשֵּׁב, וְאִי אַתָּה מְחַשֵּׁב חֳדָשִׁים.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «One does not count months» in order to lower the price to be paid to the Temple treasury, but the Temple treasury may count months in order to raise the price of redemption. With regard to this statement, «the Sages taught» in a baraita: «From where» is it derived «that one does not count months» in order to lower the price to be paid «to the Temple» treasury? «The verse states: “Then the priest shall reckon for him the money according to the years that remain» until the Jubilee Year, and a deduction shall be made from your valuation” (Leviticus 27:18). This teaches that «you» are to «calculate years, but you» are «not» to «count months.»
